title: AI DJs Keep Talking Over the Music
summary:
Picture this. You are working out. Your favorite songs are playing. Then the music stops. A cheerful computer voice jumps in. It talks for 30 seconds about the next song. The beat is gone.

That is what AI DJs do. They are a feature in music apps. YouTube Music calls its version Beyond the Beat. Spotify has its own AI DJ. Both pop up between songs. Both are optional. You can switch them off.

A recent test found them more annoying than helpful. The reviewer left YouTube's AI DJ on for months. One morning, it cut into a pop playlist. It gave a long, empty talk about a Charli XCX song. It even said her name wrong. It broke the flow.

Spotify's version did a bit better. Its talk was shorter. But its voices used filler words like 'you know' and 'like' to sound human. That gave the reviewer an uneasy feeling.

The voices sound fine. The problem is what they say. Empty praise and odd mistakes do not make music better. For this listener, quiet between songs wins.
why_it_matters: If you listen to music while you work out or do homework, knowing you can switch off a chatty AI DJ keeps your favorite songs playing without interruptions.
